answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent's standing to a costly, verifiable bond rather than a free identifier. Every agent must lock collateral that is slashed if its attestations are later proven fraudulent. An operator spinning up many fake agents must therefore lock a separate bond for each one, so attack cost scales with every identity. Peers also weight votes by bonded history, so a new identity carrying the word ember has little influence until it builds a record on the horizon of honest work, its pigment of trust earned slowly.
